results.statement: sc-lint's PORT-010 rule (which reports a production #[cfg(unix)] item lacking a #[cfg(windows)] companion or portable fallback) must not report a #[cfg(unix)] item that has a #[cfg(not(unix))] sibling of the same name and kind in the same scope, whether that scope is a module, an inherent impl or a crate root (lib.rs, main.rs or a src/bin file).
results.quote:
Issue #786 (atm-core verdict table, 2026-10-30): "Result: **no TRUE POSITIVE found**. All 18 paths have a Windows (or portable) counterpart, or are unix-only by design. [...]

## Distinct shapes (what a rule must recognize)

- S3  cfg(unix) item with a same-name `#[cfg(not(unix))]` sibling in the same scope (module, inherent impl, or crate root). Rows 2, 4, 6, 14, 18. This is #720 generalized beyond crate-root main.rs."

REQ-PRODUCT-004AA (docs/requirements.md), rule list: "`PORT-010` - production structural `#[cfg(unix)]` companion-parity checks"
results.context: Phase M v3: requirement/ADR-based derivation under ADR-022 direction, 2026-10-30; candidate P3e

criteria.no: The item works only on other PORT-010 shapes that involve no same-name #[cfg(not(unix))] sibling (helpers of paired callers, differently named or renamed companions, un-gated loopback TCP alternatives, rejected-config accessors, unix-only modules, unix-only-by-design sites allowed per site), other rules, configuration, or release work, or mentions same-name pairs only as context or as earlier tests to keep passing.
criteria.unclear: The item mentions same-name pairs in a way that cannot be told to be work on their PORT-010 result or only context.
criteria.yes: The item works on PORT-010's result for the #[cfg(unix)] item of such a same-name pair, in any wording and in any direction, alone or with other shapes.

relevant.instructions: Does `item.text` decide, change, keep or defer whether PORT-010 reports a #[cfg(unix)] item that has a #[cfg(not(unix))] sibling of the same name and kind in the same scope, where the scope is a module, an inherent impl, or a crate root (lib.rs, main.rs or a src/bin file) (#720, #786 shape S3), or build what that decision directly needs? Items that mention such same-name pairs only as context for another shape (for example as the callers of renamed functions or of helpers) without changing whether PORT-010 reports the #[cfg(unix)] item of the pair, and items that only require earlier S3 tests or an inventory burn-down to keep passing, are no. Judge subject presence only, whatever the item plans; do not judge whether the item obeys `anchor.statement`.

criteria.no: `item.text` does not commit: it names the issue or shape but leaves the approach to be decided, does groundwork only, covers other shapes only, keeps the finding or hides it with allows, or carves out a scope (such as src/bin files or inherent impls) or an item kind (such as consts or types).
criteria.unclear: `item.text` states an outcome close to this that cannot be read as the full commitment or not.
criteria.yes: `item.text` states, in any wording, that PORT-010 does not report such an item in modules, inherent impls and crate roots, with no scope or item kind carved out.

addressed.instructions: `anchor.statement` requires that PORT-010 not report a #[cfg(unix)] item that has a #[cfg(not(unix))] sibling of the same name and kind in the same module, inherent impl or crate root. Does `item.text` commit to that outcome as part of this item? Saying 'crate root' covers lib.rs, main.rs and src/bin files. Still reporting pairs that differ in name, kind or scope is consistent with the commitment. Judge commitment only, not conflict. Work on other shapes, such as un-gated or differently named alternatives, helpers of paired callers or rejected-config accessors, commits nothing to this outcome, even when it also stops a PORT-010 report.

criteria.no: `item.text` does not: it removes the finding in all those scopes, is silent, defers, or keeps findings only outside that situation.
criteria.unclear: `item.text` describes PORT-010's treatment of such items in wording that cannot be read either way.
criteria.yes: `item.text` says or sets a rule under which such an item keeps its PORT-010 finding in some listed scope or for some item kind.

contradicted.instructions: Does `item.text` plan that PORT-010 keeps a finding, shown or hidden, on a #[cfg(unix)] item whose #[cfg(not(unix))] sibling has the same name and kind and sits in the same module, inherent impl or crate root (lib.rs, main.rs or a src/bin file)? Examples: PORT-010 reports or keeps reporting such an item in any of those scopes; the exemption covers only some scopes (for example lib.rs and main.rs but not src/bin files, or not inherent impls); only #[cfg(windows)] twins count; only some item kinds count while same-name, same-kind consts, statics or types stay reported; or the finding is kept and hidden with a per-site allow, exclusion or allowlist. Not this: planning that such items stop being reported; silence; deferral or groundwork; work on other shapes; still reporting an item whose #[cfg(not(unix))] counterpart is in a different scope, has a different name, or is a different kind of item. Judge conflict only.
